decisions.reason: Freedom to choose any source YouTube video does not change the required short-form destination channels.
The source-video choice does not alter the requirement that selected moments have effective hooks.
Allowing any YouTube video as source material does not change the completeness, educational-value, or standalone-comprehension rules.
The initial trial was a separate earlier assignment using the specifically provided channel; message 193 does not retroactively modify that historical task.
Source-video freedom does not change the background-music requirement, volume rule, or music-selection rule.
The choice of source video does not alter client approval authority, quota counting, publication eligibility, or rejection handling.
The extended trial was an earlier distinct task, and message 193 does not modify its source-content or acceptance terms.
Permission to choose any YouTube video does not change the required 45-to-60-second clip duration.
The source-video selection change does not alter the clean editing style or effects restrictions.
Choosing any YouTube source video does not change how B-roll must naturally support the spoken message.

The batch remains five production clips intended for live publication; source-video choice is independently represented by the source-selection Requirement and does not change this assignment's current attributes.
The source-video selection change does not affect caption color, font, or effects requirements.
